draft.title: Coping flexibility
card: Coping flexibility is the ability to notice when a coping strategy is not working and to switch to a different one.
No single strategy suits every stressor. A strategy that helps in one situation may not help in another.
A flexible coper checks the result of what they are doing. If the stress stays high, they try something else that fits the situation.
A person who keeps using the same strategy, even when it is not working, has low coping flexibility.
draft.remember: Coping well means checking if a strategy works and changing it when it does not.

a.q: Which person is showing coping flexibility?
opts: Ravi sees extra study is not helping and asks his teacher
Ravi uses one study timetable every term, whatever happens
Ravi picks the strategy his friend says works best for him
Ravi avoids thinking about his exam until the night before
a.why: Ravi notices that his strategy is not working and switches to a different one. Using the same timetable regardless of results is the opposite, because it ignores whether the strategy helps.
a.clue: Look for noticing a strategy is failing, then changing it.

b.q: Mei calms herself before swimming races by going for a long run. When a knee injury stops her running, she still tries to run and her stress rises. What does this show?
opts: Low coping flexibility, as she did not switch strategy
High coping flexibility, as she kept her strategy
Running is always a poor way to cope with stress
Mei has no stress response to a change in her situation
b.why: A strategy that worked before no longer suits her situation, and Mei did not switch to another. That is low coping flexibility. Running is not poor in itself: it helped her before, so it is wrong to say it never works.
b.clue: Did Mei change her strategy when the situation changed?

a.best: Ravi sees extra study is not helping and asks his teacher

b.best: Low coping flexibility, as she did not switch strategy
